To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the modular symmetry group of a local net of observables in de Sitter space is the conformal group, while that of a local net on a Robertson-Walker space-time is larger than the conformal group.

1) The modular groups of local nets on the Robertson-Walker space times are generically larger that their isometry and conformals groups; 2) The modular groups are stable under small perturbations of the Robertson-Walker metric, and; 3) The modular action is geometric, in the sense that it is implemented by geometric diffeomorphisms of the underlying manifold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction and analysis of local nets of von Neumann algebras on Robertson-Walker space-time.
the following question: What are the consequences of imposing the condition of geometric modular actions on the algebras of local observables in Robertson-Walker space times?
the question of whether there is a natural class of local observables on a given space-time which are invariant under the modular symmetry group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the Robertson-Walker space-time, the modular symmetry group is the conformal group of the space-time, and that this group is not the same as the isometry group.

the geometric modular action condition, together with the condition of modular stability (or the condition of positivity of the modular Hamiltonian), provides a natural and satisfactory replacement for the energy condition in Minkowski and de Sitter space.
the geometric modular action is a natural, and in some sense universal, property of local nets of algebras of quantum observables on Robertson-Walker space-time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modular symmetry of the local algebras in de Sitter space can be extended to a large class Robertson-Walker space-time.
the modular symmetry of a quantum field theory is a more general concept than the symmetry group of the underlying space-time.

the geometric modular action condition, in conjunction with a suitable version of the Reeh-Schlieder theorem, is a viable alternative to the energy condition as a means to single out the physically relevant local nets on Robertson-Walker space-time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existence of geometric modular action is a robust feature of quantum field theory in curved spacetime.
, for the Robertson-Walker space-time, the modular symmetry group is larger than the isometries and conformal symmetries.
the existence of a large class of local nets of observables which comply with a condition of geometric modular symmetry is a robust feature of space-time geometry.
